questions.q: Why don't the raw Chicago and Hanoi sign-in records, by themselves, indicate an attack?
options: Sign-in records are never reliable enough to be trusted on their own
They're just two normalized authentication records from Chapter 3's collection pipeline - correlation is what gives them meaning
Windows Event Forwarding only delivers logs for failed logins
The domain controller and mail platform use incompatible log formats
questions.explain: Individual log records are neutral; Chapter 4's correlation logic is what turns two ordinary records into a meaningful alert.

questions.q: What does Lesson 30's correlation rule specifically contribute to this case?
options: It automatically resets the compromised account's password
It prevents Tier 2 from ever needing to investigate the case
It ties the login pair and the mailbox rule change into one composite, higher-severity alert instead of two separate ones
It only works on accounts belonging to company directors
questions.explain: The composite alert is what makes the incident visible as one serious event rather than two lower-priority, easier-to-miss alerts.

questions.q: Why does Jordan escalate to Tier 2 instead of investigating the case further alone?
options: Escalation is required any time a login occurs outside business hours
Tier 1 analysts are not permitted to write case notes
Tier 1's role is fast, accurate judgment on whether to escalate - the deeper audit-trail and lateral-sweep work is Tier 2's job
The SIEM automatically locks Tier 1 out of escalated alerts
questions.explain: The division of labor exists because Tier 1 triage and Tier 2 investigation require different depth and different time budgets.

questions.q: Why does the SOAR playbook in Step 6 run only after the analyst's judgment call, rather than making that call itself?
options: SOAR platforms are technically incapable of running without human approval of every single action
It keeps human judgment in the decision step while automating the repeatable, lower-risk execution steps
Playbooks can only run during business hours
Automating the decision step is faster than automating the execution step
questions.explain: The analyst confirms what happened; the playbook only executes the already-decided containment actions, which is the safer division.

questions.q: How does this single case affect the Chapter 6 dashboard metrics?
options: It permanently lowers the SOC's average detection time for all future cases
It produces a fast MTTD from the composite alert, a longer but appropriate MTTR from the fuller investigation, and a line in the leadership report
It has no measurable effect on any dashboard metric
It only affects metrics if the incident involves a data breach notification
questions.explain: Every stage of the case - detection, escalation, resolution - is timestamped and feeds directly into MTTD, MTTR, and the weekly report.
